newsitem.title: USA: U.S. watching Zaire in case pullout needed - Cohen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. watching Zaire in case pullout needed - Cohen.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Friday that U.S. officials were monitoring the rebellion in Zaire day by day, even hour by hour, to assess whether to evacuate U.S. citizens.
"We are in the preparatorial stage to make sure we can act if action is called for," Cohen told reporters.

When asked if he believed evacuation would be needed, Cohen said "that depends on a day by day assessment, it could be an hour by hour assessment, that we are following very closely and as usual we will take every measure possible to make sure our citizens are safe."

Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon said on Thursday the United States military was making contingency preparations to evacuate Americans from Zaire if necessary. France has already sent troops and planes to nearby Gabon and Congo in case evacuations are needed.
Rebels who have been fighting since October to try to topple Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko seized Zaire's third city of Kisangani over the weekend.
Mobutu left France where he had undergone cancer treatment for home on Friday in an effort to salvage control of the Central African country.
But Laurent Kabila's rebels rejected a call for a ceasefire and then peace negotiations. "We negotiate first," Kabila said on arrival in Kisangani.
